target_customer: Web publishers wanting revenue beyond ads and subscriptions, and readers buying single articles
problem: Ad blockers and subscription fatigue cut publisher revenue; CoinTent let readers pay for single articles with one click on the publisher's own site.
business_model: Payment processing fee per micropayment transaction, sized by transaction

founders.name: Brad Ross
prior_employers: Zynga (micropayments for games, per team description)
founders.background_notes: Digital Commerce 360 (2015-04) says the founding team previously pioneered micropayments for millions of Zynga games users.

founders.name: Bigi Lui
prior_employers: Zynga (architect and founding engineer on Mafia Wars)
founders.background_notes: Employers as listed on the YC page bio.

founders.name: Kendra Gibbons
founders.background_notes: YC page lists her as a founder with no bio.

competitors.name: Blendle
competitors.what: Dutch platform for buying individual articles from many publishers, with a 30 percent cut and instant refunds
competitors.traction_then: Over 1 million users and US launch in 2016
competitors.funding_then: $3.8M in 2014 from the New York Times and Axel Springer

competitors.name: Flattr
competitors.what: Monthly budget tipping service launched in 2010 that splits money among publishers the user flattrs
competitors.traction_then: Struggled to gain adoption with major publishers

competitors.name: Tibit
competitors.what: London micropayment tool for small donations on publisher sites, product ready in June 2016
competitors.funding_then: About $175K crowdfunded and $150K private as of June 2016

technical_complexity.rationale: A payments wallet, API and WordPress plugin require secure transaction handling and publisher integration, but use standard web technology.

defensibility.rationale: A shared wallet could create network effects across sites, but with only 25 beta sites and easy rivals it was not established.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Micropayment rivals such as Blendle later shut their micropayment models per 2016 and later press; no source describes incumbents copying CoinTent.

market_need_then: Digital Commerce 360 (2015-04) reported beta publishers saw 2 to 5 times as many paying viewers and a 55 percent one click spend rate across more than 25 sites. Ad blocker adoption cut ad revenue, and CEO Ross later described CoinTent as covering ad block detection and reader rendezvous.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline: Recover revenue lost to ad blockers (YC page).

brand_strength.rationale: The wordplay on coin and content explains the product, but press covered it mainly as a funding and launch item, and the name was easy to confuse with crypto products.

pivots.to: Ad blocker recovery and reader liberation tools
pivots.why: A 2016 article quoted the CEO describing an ad block detection suite; the YC tagline also focuses on ad blocker revenue.

outcome_analysis: CoinTent raised a $1.075M seed in April 2015 from Foundry Group and angels and ran a beta on over 25 sites, then joined YC in Summer 2016 with a shift toward ad blocker revenue recovery. The YC page marks it inactive but no source states a shutdown or reason, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty. Micropayments for content were a hard category for peers like Blendle.
notes: The seed is stated by two outlets (Digital Commerce 360 and PYMNTS). The company website safety check was rate limited so cointent.com was not read. The 2016 pivot comes from a search summary of an article quoting the CEO, which I did not open. FIPP does not mention CoinTent; it is used for the category rivals. Outcome searches found no shutdown or acquisition report, only other micropayment companies closing.
